chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Last days in Los Angeles; Pagani's publicity and "El Bongo Arrollador"
summary: Federico Pagani handled publicity and set up twenty or so live broadcasts; they recorded the Bongo number with Verne.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Yes. Well, we finished. We took Federico Pagani on vacation.
Was he out there for three months?

Three months with us and then when we came back here he stayed there about another three months because, you know, he is smart in publicity and propaganda or whatever you want to call it and he stayed there. He helped us a lot because he helped to make the publicity; so all the posters and - you name it - he was the one to incite the guy to put a broadcasting in order to publicize.....
Oh, yes! So then he is the one that set up that remote broadcasting, eh? How many live broadcasts did you make from the Club Brazil, do you remember?
Could be about twenty or twenty-five.
W O W!! All right, you came back here, you met Betty Riley, you made that short for the movie, 'El Bongo Arrollador'. Were you still recording for Verne at the time?
... and we made 'El Bongo Arrollador', with Verne.
Right. Okay, did you record 'El Bongo' Arrollador' after you recorded it for Verne or before?
Ahh - Can't remember, I think we recorded after.
